messages:
alex: hey folks, first-day 👋. running into a few small bootstrapping things on my new M2: installed asdf and used the org's dotfiles-starter, brewed openssl, installed node 20 and python 3.11. two problems: 1) some npm native modules fail with node-gyp missing OpenSSL, 2) direnv loads but my REPO_TOKEN isn't picked up in VS Code's integrated terminal. any quick pointers?

priya: welcome! quick checklist: make sure /opt/homebrew/bin is first in PATH, set CPPFLAGS/LDFLAGS for brew openssl, and reshim asdf after installs. for VS Code, ensure the app inherits your login shell env (open via terminal or use code --enable-proposed-api? jk). specifically what do you see for the REPO_TOKEN env?

alex: npm error: "gyp ERR! stack Error: Can't find OpenSSL include directory". REPO_TOKEN shows in a normal Terminal but not in VS Code terminal (which opens a non-login shell apparently).

dan: for node-gyp do: `brew install openssl@1.1 pkg-config` then in ~/.zprofile add:
```bash
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"
export LDFLAGS="-L/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/lib"
export CPPFLAGS="-I/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@1.1/include"
. $HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh
```
then restart and `rm -rf node_modules && npm ci`. For VS Code: set "terminal.integrated.inheritEnv": true (it usually is) and make sure you launch VS Code from the dock AFTER updating ~/.zprofile, or run `open -a 'Visual Studio Code'` from a terminal so it inherits the login environment.

priya: for direnv + REPO_TOKEN we recommend storing secrets in macOS Keychain and exposing via a small loader in ~/.zprofile instead of committing to dotfiles. Example: `export REPO_TOKEN="$(security find-generic-password -s redwood-repo -w)"` and allow direnv in the repo .envrc to read that. Then both Terminal and apps launched from a terminal will get it.

alex: ah ok — I had put the exports only in ~/.zshrc. moving brew/path/openssl exports to ~/.zprofile fixed the node-gyp build locally. VS Code still didn't pick it up until I relaunched the app via `open -a 'Visual Studio Code'` from Terminal. thanks!

dan: one more gotcha: if you're using the Homebrew-installed git and ssh, ensure which git/ssh point to /opt/homebrew ones. Also if you use SSH agent + keychain: `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` and add these lines to ~/.ssh/config:
```text
Host *
  AddKeysToAgent yes
  UseKeychain yes
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
```
That keeps your key loaded across restarts and makes git clones seamless.

alex: ssh keychain saved me — and REPO_TOKEN now visible in VS Code too. last micro Q: the starter dotfiles uses stow and a setup script that symlinks `.envrc.example` -> `.envrc`. should I copy secrets into `.envrc` or use direnv + keychain?

priya: never commit secrets. Copying into local `.envrc` is OK if it's excluded from git and you keep it local, but we prefer keychain + direnv so you don't accidentally echo tokens. If you'd like, ping me and I'll add you to the dotfiles repo team so you can push a tiny change or open a PR for any improvements.

infra-bot: Reminder: new-hire setup hangout tomorrow 2:00pm PT in #onboarding-office-hours for live help. :calendar:

alex: perfect, everything green now. huge thanks! I'll tidy my zprofile and push a short note to the dotfiles PR if I add a small helper script.
